accuracy.evidence: The content follows the PSHE Association Programme of Study (2020) key stage 1 health and wellbeing strand (what they are good at, what they find difficult, managing when things are hard), the DfE Health Education guidance (2019) on self-respect and mental wellbeing, and the EYFS Self-Regulation goal (set and work towards simple goals). The goal advice (a specific goal such as five catches in a row beats 'get better' or 'do your best') is the Locke and Latham (2002) finding. The adult text does not oversell mindset talk: it says mindset messages alone show small effects (Sisk et al. 2018) and that the work is practice with a clear goal. Parameterised sums checked at their corners: 1+1 to 4+4, 2+1 to 4+3, 2+1 to 5+4, and 4-1 to 6-3 (never negative).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the real slips for this age: practising means bad at it (prediction 1 and the 'notyet' refusal when a practising card goes to Good at), modesty that hides a real strength (a good-at card dropped in Practising is refused with 'saying so is not showing off'), grown-ups are good at everything (prediction 2; Dad and Miss Khan each have a practising chip), put-down self-talk as 'just being honest' (prediction 3), 'I'm not good at anything' (refused on the own-board words), and goals that are about beating others, perfect, vague or too big (four refused goal cards, each with its own reason).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagstrength is built on this topic's own moves: evidence-based sorting of one child's abilities into good at now versus still practising, a four-person panel where each person (two of them adults) has exactly one practising chip, a speech-bubble swap of put-downs for practising words matched to the right skill, a goal board that only takes small, clear, self-referenced goals, and a personal board with kind-words choice. It differs from 248 flaglike (likes and jobs I can do alone), 388 flagprac (repeated tries get neater) and 157 flagtry (persisting after a mistake); the 6-token shingle gate reports no flag lab above 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: The rule is found by doing: Swimming bounces off Good at it now with 'he can't do this every time yet', so the every-time test is discovered; tapping a strong chip for Dad is refused until the guitar chip is found, so 'grown-ups practise too' is seen, not told; the bubble only changes and Sam only smiles when a practising phrase for that same skill is dropped; the goal board refuses 'Get better' until a clear goal is chosen. Each DONE line then states the rule.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions, each with a tempting wrong option that the scene disproves: 'Yes, he is bad at it' (the swimming card belongs in Still practising), 'No, grown-ups are good at everything' (all four people, including Dad and Miss Khan, have a practising chip), 'Yes, it is just being honest' (the put-down is swapped and Sam smiles and keeps going), and 'Be the best in the class' (that card is refused on the goal board). The reveal line names the right answer after the task.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven questions; every wrong option maps to a named slip, checked with chal.cjs after fixing two mismatches found on the first click-through: 'bad' (still practising is not bad at it), 'never2', 'showoff', 'onlygrown' (children can know their strengths too), 'grownup', 'nobody', 'giveup', 'compare', 'best', 'vague', 'kit' (Kit can name things Kit does well) and 'hide'. Double full stops after answers ending in a quote were also fixed.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences and everyday examples (bike, cat drawing, laces, guitar) and pass the family kid limit; adult paragraphs name the PSHE, DfE, EYFS and goal-setting basis in plain words inside the adult limit (validators pass). Canvas cards are short, e.g. 'Sam catches 2 balls out of 10', and headings are one line.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs: good at (every time), practising (some of the time, not bad at), everyone has both, kind words plus one small goal. Adult paragraphs: curriculum basis, the evidence test and goal research, named common mistakes plus a caution about praise, and what to do at home. The content gate finds no filler phrase and no text above 12% overlap with another lesson.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px phone screenshots in light and dark for all five scenes plus the challenge: six Sam cards in a 2 x 3 grid above two bins with icon and label, four person panels in a 2 x 2 grid with three readable chips each, the put-down bubble beside Sam above six kind-word cards, the two goal slots holding 'Catch the ball 5 times in a row' on three lines without clipping, and the own board with twelve skill chips in a 3 x 4 grid. Real mouse drags (card to bin, words to bubble, chip to zone) worked at 390 px.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: 'Good at: Bike' / 'Practising: Bike' with full-text aria-labels, one button per person's chip ('Is Dad still practising playing the guitar?'), one per kind-words card and goal card, 'Good at: Drawing' / 'Practising: Drawing' for the own board, and one per words choice. The canvas aria-label carries each scene description and all feedback; challenge feedback is a role=status live region; ticks, crosses, stars and sprouts mark state as well as colour; axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) is clean in both themes in the browser gate.

sources: PSHE Association (2020) Programme of Study for PSHE Education, Key stages 1 to 5: KS1 health and wellbeing (what they are good at, finding things difficult)
DfE (2019) Relationships Education, Relationships and Sex Education and Health Education: statutory guidance (mental wellbeing, self-respect)
DfE (2021) Statutory framework for the EYFS: ELG Self-Regulation (set and work towards simple goals)
Locke, E. A. and Latham, G. P. (2002) Building a practically useful theory of goal setting and task motivation, American Psychologist 57(9)
Sisk, V. F. et al. (2018) To what extent and under which circumstances are growth mind-sets important to academic achievement? Psychological Science 29(4)
